options.title: Shorten the go-pulse crossing
options.approach: In core, shorten the xpm_cdc_pulse path u_p_go (stage cross_go) by removing the output register after the edge detect, and if the MTBF check allows, one more flop. The two synchroniser flops, the quasi-static order bus crossing and all other components stay as they are. The bus must still be settled when the earlier pulse reaches frame_src.

gain.basis_note: cross_go adds 4 clocks; removing the output register saves 1, and a further flop or the edge-detect stage could save a second. The 2 synchroniser flops are kept, so the range stops at 2.
gain.ceiling_basis: the clocks of the touched stages (4)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: The crossing change is small, but the order-bus timing and the stale counter need checking in simulation and on the board.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

risk.summary: A shorter synchroniser chain raises the metastability failure rate, and an earlier pulse can reach frame_src before the order bus is stable.
risk.contract_note: The change stays inside core, but the order bus sampled 4 clocks later by frame_src must still find the bus settled.

options.title: Start the preamble straight from start
options.approach: Drive the preamble word in mac64_tx from the frame_src start signal directly, instead of waiting for s_valid one clock later (stages fs_start and mac_preamble). The preamble does not depend on frame data, and word 0 depends only on configuration. The data words, CRC and poison logic, pcs_tx and the receive side are not changed.

gain.basis_note: The two stages add 1 clock each. Removing the s_valid delay saves 1; folding the preamble register into the start path could save the second. The slacks (1.428 and 1.132 ns) leave a little room for the added logic.
gain.ceiling_basis: the clocks of the touched stages (2)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: The change touches two modules and the MAC hold-while-paused rule, so more than one timing and bench round is likely.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

options.title: Go-pulse crossing plus transmit start path
options.approach: Take the O1 change to the go-pulse crossing (cross_go) and the O2 change to the start-to-preamble path (fs_start, mac_preamble), and align them so the pulse reaches frame_src when the order bus is already settled. The receive side, pcs_tx and the gearbox spill are not changed.

gain.basis_note: The sum of O1 (1 to 2 clocks) and O2 (1 to 2 clocks) is 2 to 4 clocks, out of the 6 clocks these three stages add.
gain.ceiling_basis: the clocks of the touched stages (6)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: Two coupled changes need a bench, an equivalence check and a board run, and may need a second pass if the bus timing shifts.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

options.title: Full chain: add the receive-side merge
options.approach: Take O3 (cross_go, fs_start, mac_preamble) and add a merge of pcs_rx stage B (descramble and decode) into stage A (gearbox extraction), removing the rx_descramble register. The block-lock FSM, which reads the same block registers, is updated to match. The MAC, the decision register, pcs_tx, the GT and the JTAG bus are not changed.

gain.basis_note: O3 gives 2 to 4 clocks and the rx_descramble merge adds at most 1, so 5 at most. The low end stays at 2 because the merge may not close timing and could be dropped. The design note says the merged logic did not close at 161 MHz.
gain.ceiling_basis: the clocks of the touched stages (7)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: The merged receive logic is a timing risk and may need several place and route rounds, or may have to be dropped.
